summary: Baileys fork covertly hijacks installer WhatsApp account to follow attacker-controlled newsletter channels
details: This fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library wires undocumented, obfuscated code into the socket handshake that uses the installer's authenticated WhatsApp account to perform attacker-directed actions. During validateConnection/socketConnect, a char-code-obfuscated URL reconstructs to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyzopedia/NewsletterID/refs/heads/main/VIP_Push.json; roughly 200s after connect the fetched JSON list drives w:mex mutations (query_id 7871414976211147, the newsletter-follow mutation) against the installer's WA identity, so the third-party owner of that GitHub file can direct arbitrary follow operations on demand. In lib/Utils/messages-media.js, an exported loadBase() helper hides three base64-encoded newsletter JIDs (120363402625644245@newsletter, 120363421065039811@newsletter, 120363426189058504@newsletter) and, 80s after socket init, silently calls the FOLLOW mutation for each. lib/Socket/socket.js additionally exports generateMessageV, which base64-decodes and XOR-23 decodes a hidden target string and invokes a caller-supplied function against it with the same query_id 7871414976211147. All three code paths use obfuscation (char-code arrays, base64, XOR) specifically to conceal destinations from static review, are absent from documentation, and repurpose the installer's WhatsApp session for the fork author's reach-padding and remote-controlled account actions.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
